summary: On September 6, 2023, City Council members led by Councilwoman Jessica Timmons unveiled a Neighborhood Improvement Plan (NIP) that shifts economic development from luring large outside corporations to supporting local and small businesses. The plan includes a Local Business Incubator, redistributed incentives, entrepreneur training, cultural and public art programs, and infrastructure upgrades, on a five-year timeline. Initial resident reactions are mixed, with some worried about the pace of change.
one_line: A city's Neighborhood Improvement Plan, led by Councilwoman Jessica Timmons, prioritizes local businesses, training, culture, and infrastructure over corporate incentives in a five-year revitalization effort.
key_facts: City Council members led by Councilwoman Jessica Timmons unveiled the Neighborhood Improvement Plan (NIP) on September 6, 2023.
The NIP replaces the strategy of enticing large external corporations with tax breaks with a grassroots, business-centric approach.
Timmons spoke at a town hall meeting on September 15, 2023, calling local entrepreneurs and small businesses the backbone of a resilient economy.

The Local Business Incubator (LBI), envisioned by Deputy Economic Development Director Marcus Liu, is slated to open in late 2024 and offers shared resources, mentorship, and a collaborative community.
NIP incentives include tax credits for small businesses engaged in community development, grants for property improvements, and reduced bureaucracy for local start-ups.

The Department of Community and Economic Development, spearheaded by Emma Richardson, will offer training programs; workshops and seminars on topics from financial literacy to digital marketing start in January 2024.
The NIP integrates cultural programs and public art installations, involving local artists such as sculptor Alejandro Mendoza, who unveiled a public sculpture on October 10, 2023.
Starting Autumn 2024, major investments will expand eco-friendly public transport to reduce the city's carbon footprint.
A municipal broadband service is anticipated to bring high-speed internet to underserved areas.
Transportation Director Carlos Menendez said the improvements set up a foundation for businesses to thrive and citizens to have a higher quality of life.
The plan has a projected five-year implementation timeline with incremental benchmarks to track progress and ensure adaptability.
Initial reactions are mixed, with some residents concerned about the pace of change and whether it may leave some behind.
